The values in v3a.note are approved (D144, and its follow-up the same day for spendCapUsdPerWindow); the price-path seeds are drawn at freeze and only their hashes go here.
units: USDC and AGU-lab in base units (6 decimals); face in mSIU; rates in nano-USD per SIU; basis points for shares; ppm for price-path volatility

reserve.bufferNote: D146 (owner, 2026-11-12, amends D144): v3a has no finite buffer. An open-ended lab subsidy pays each roll's cover for unsold front work when it falls due; the board shows what it has paid so far beside the shadow NAV, the scorer reports the total per run, and D144's buffer gate is gone. Seed and target are zero so no buffer is ever seeded or refilled (carry goes to income).

issuers.reason: Owner, D143 and D144: X passes at D119's 80% qualifying floor on CR-PL, CR-UO and CR-SM (a pre-registered rule, not a measured cell: the trial's weakest qualifying cell, sonnet-5 on CR-PL at 9 of 10, is statistically indistinguishable from C1/C2 and would leave the claims record with no defaults to show) and lists 15% below C1/C2. X is cheaper per task; since failed work pays nothing (v6), its cost is not price but timing risk: a failed task burns rounds, and with 8 rounds a window that can make a need lapse. Its pass rate is in the pass-rate table; failShareBps stays 0 because the table already carries the rate.

claude-sonnet-5 serves all four task types by commission (design, Issuers table); it bonds claim lots for CR-VS only, so no Commodity reserve claim can be routed to a Frontier issuer (the routing rule params.ts checks).

v3a.note: APPROVED by the owner (D144): mandates' minValueBufferBps (cautious 4000, standard 2500, permissive 1000); sweep shareOfStartingValueBps 1500 (15% of starting value per sweep, demand agents only); printPath.classNoisePpm 2000 (0.2% a day); dataPriceMilli 148 (the mean of the three Commodity class prices, 301, 58 and 86 mSIU); providerRules (discount from -20% to +50%, offers up to 3 windows ahead, a default costs PROVIDER the bond's payout once); minRedeemMilli and minCreateMilli 250; hedger.briefsSold 8 (one a window); minCounts; reserve buffer 1.5 USDC (seed and target; a validity gate fails the run if it runs dry before the end of window 8); coder models gpt-5.1 and claude-haiku-5-5; spendCapUsdPerWindow 2.00 (D144 follow-up, 2026-11-12: an API-cost safety stop on the model agents' spend in each window, not a limit on any agent). Fixed by the design or the owner: everything else.

v3a.capacityNote: D145 (owner, 2026-11-12): each reserve-grade issuer (C1, C2, X) commits 2 windows of its measured rate (v6: capacity = committed hours x measured rate; a bigger bond never raises issuance, C6). Sized from the four scripted cells (arms A and B, low and high volatility; price seeds shadow-check-<arm>-<vol>, run seeds shadow-<arm>-<vol>), run 2026-11-12 with 1000 hours so the limit could not bind: the largest live issuance relative to capacity was CR-PL in arm B high (run v3a-scripted-armB-high-2026-11-12T13-01-28-706Z), 20,516 mSIU against the issuers' 29,018 mSIU per hour, so twice that peak needs 1.41 hours; 2 is the smallest whole number covering it (2.83x in that run, more in the others). The largest live issuance in absolute terms was 28,176 mSIU of CR-PL in arm A high, against 50,372 mSIU per hour there. Live issuance counts the reserve and every other live claim on the same capacity (PROVIDER's sales), so it is at least the reserve. The issuers' measured rate varies with the print at genesis; v6's issuance limit stays in code and a validity gate fails any run in which it binds.
